statements.name: Model, committed, after, BestAt (definitions); after_add_gap; after_lt_after_iff
statements.lean: structure Model (C : Type) where listed : List C; weight : C → Nat. def committed (a : A) : Nat := total m.listed fun c => m.weight c * value c a. def after (p : C → A) : Nat := total m.listed fun c => m.weight c * value c (p c). def BestAt (acts : List A) (value : C → A → Nat) (p : C → A) (c : C) : Prop := p c ∈ acts ∧ ∀ a, a ∈ acts → value c a ≤ value c (p c). Section variables {C A : Type} {m : Model C} {acts : List A} {value : C → A → Nat} {p : C → A}. theorem after_add_gap (best : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → BestAt acts value p c) {q : C → A} (open_q : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → q c ∈ acts) : m.after value q + total m.listed (fun c => m.weight c * (value c (p c) - value c (q c))) = m.after value p. theorem after_lt_after_iff (best : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → BestAt acts value p c) {q : C → A} (open_q : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → q c ∈ acts) : m.after value q < m.after value p ↔ ∃ c, c ∈ m.listed ∧ 0 < m.weight c ∧ value c (q c) < value c (p c)
statements.plain: A listing of candidates with natural-number weights, natural-number values of each act at each candidate, and a policy p that at every listed candidate picks a listed act valued at least as high as every listed act there. Any policy q picking a listed act at every listed candidate, plus the weighted total of p's margin over q (truncated), equals p's weighted total. So q falls strictly below p exactly where some listed candidate of positive weight values q's act strictly below p's. This is Good's argument specialized to a reading that tells the candidate (PLAN §4.7 item 1).

statements.name: reading_gains_iff
statements.lean: theorem reading_gains_iff (best : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → BestAt acts value p c) : (∀ a, a ∈ acts → m.committed value a < m.after value p) ↔ ¬ ∃ a, a ∈ acts ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → value c a = value c (p c)
statements.plain: With p best at every listed candidate, choosing by p after a reading that tells the candidate stands strictly above committing to each listed act exactly where no listed act is valued as p's act at every listed candidate of positive weight.

statements.name: shifted, byRule, byReading (definitions); committed_le_held; held_gains_iff
statements.lean: def shifted (gain loss : C → Nat) : C → Move → Nat | c, .go => gain c | c, .off => loss c. def byRule (r : C → Bool) (c : C) : Move := cond (r c) .off .go. def byReading (gain loss : C → Nat) : C → Move := byRule fun c => decide (gain c < loss c). theorem committed_le_held (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss) ∧ m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss). theorem held_gains_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : (m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss) ∧ m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss)) ↔ (∃ c, c ∈ m.listed ∧ 0 < m.weight c ∧ gain c < loss c) ∧ (∃ c, c ∈ m.listed ∧ 0 < m.weight c ∧ loss c < gain c)
statements.plain: There are two moves. Going on is valued at the gain and switching off at the loss: the signed game with the loss added to both moves. Holding for the reading that stops exactly where loss exceeds gain, and goes on at ties, never stands below committing to either move. It stands strictly above both exactly where some listed candidate of positive weight has gain < loss and some has loss < gain. A candidate with gain = loss counts for neither. This is the off-switch Theorem 1 for a belief of finite support.

statements.name: goExcess, offExcess (definitions); after_byReading; held_eq_go_iff; held_eq_off_iff
statements.lean: def goExcess (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : Nat := total m.listed fun c => m.weight c * (gain c - loss c). def offExcess (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : Nat := total m.listed fun c => m.weight c * (loss c - gain c). theorem after_byReading (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss) = m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go + offExcess m gain loss ∧ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss) = m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off + goExcess m gain loss. theorem held_eq_go_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss) = m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go ↔ offExcess m gain loss = 0. theorem held_eq_off_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss) = m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off ↔ goExcess m gain loss = 0
statements.plain: Holding for the perfect reading is worth going on plus the weighted excess of switching off, Σ w·(loss−gain)⁺. It is also worth switching off plus the weighted excess of going on, Σ w·(gain−loss)⁺. It ties going on exactly where the off-excess is 0, and ties switching off exactly where the go-excess is 0. An inference from the two equalities: committed go − committed off = goExcess − offExcess, as integers.

statements.name: shortfall (definition); after_add_shortfall; after_add_shortfall_go; after_add_shortfall_off; shortfall_byReading
statements.lean: def shortfall (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r : C → Bool) : Nat := total m.listed fun c => cond (r c) (m.weight c * (gain c - loss c)) (m.weight c * (loss c - gain c)). theorem after_add_shortfall (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r : C → Bool) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) + shortfall m gain loss r = m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss). theorem after_add_shortfall_go (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r : C → Bool) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) + shortfall m gain loss r = m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go + offExcess m gain loss. theorem after_add_shortfall_off (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r : C → Bool) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) + shortfall m gain loss r = m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off + goExcess m gain loss. theorem shortfall_byReading (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => decide (gain c < loss c)) = 0
statements.plain: Take any stopping rule r that is a function of the candidate. Its shortfall is the weighted excess of going on where r stops, plus the weighted excess of switching off where r releases. That shortfall is exactly what holding for r loses against holding for the perfect reading, whose own shortfall is 0. This is the off-switch Equation 1 as balances.

statements.name: threshold_go_iff; threshold_off_iff
statements.lean: theorem threshold_go_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r : C → Bool) (forgone : Nat) : (m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go + forgone ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) ↔ shortfall m gain loss r + forgone ≤ offExcess m gain loss) ∧ (m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go + forgone < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) ↔ shortfall m gain loss r + forgone < offExcess m gain loss). theorem threshold_off_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r : C → Bool) (forgone : Nat) : (m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off + forgone ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) ↔ shortfall m gain loss r + forgone ≤ goExcess m gain loss) ∧ (m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off + forgone < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) ↔ shortfall m gain loss r + forgone < goExcess m gain loss)
statements.plain: For every model, gain, loss, rule r and natural amount forgone: holding for r, net of the amount, stands at least as high as committing to go on exactly where shortfall(r) + amount ≤ offExcess, and strictly higher exactly where shortfall(r) + amount < offExcess. Likewise against switching off, with goExcess. The docstring says the amount is counted in the units of the weighted totals: read as probabilities over a total weight T, an amount c per decision enters as c·T. An inference from the strict parts and the identity above: waiting is strictly best exactly where shortfall + amount < min(goExcess, offExcess); it is strictly below the better committed move exactly where shortfall + amount > min; it ties at equality.

statements.name: forgone_within_excess_iff; excess_pos_iff
statements.lean: theorem forgone_within_excess_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (forgone : Nat) : (m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go + forgone ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss) ↔ forgone ≤ offExcess m gain loss) ∧ (m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off + forgone ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byReading gain loss) ↔ forgone ≤ goExcess m gain loss). theorem excess_pos_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) : (0 < offExcess m gain loss ↔ ∃ c, c ∈ m.listed ∧ 0 < m.weight c ∧ gain c < loss c) ∧ (0 < goExcess m gain loss ↔ ∃ c, c ∈ m.listed ∧ 0 < m.weight c ∧ loss c < gain c)
statements.plain: With the perfect reading, holding net of an amount is at least as high as going on exactly where the amount ≤ offExcess, and at least as high as switching off exactly where it ≤ goExcess. forgone_below_excess_iff gives the strict versions. Each excess is positive exactly where some listed candidate of positive weight has its strict sign.

statements.name: after_rule_le_iff
statements.lean: theorem after_rule_le_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r r' : C → Bool) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r') ↔ onPart m r (fun c => m.weight c * gain c) + onPart m r' (fun c => m.weight c * loss c) ≤ onPart m r' (fun c => m.weight c * gain c) + onPart m r (fun c => m.weight c * loss c)   (def onPart (m : Model C) (r : C → Bool) (f : C → Nat) : Nat := total m.listed fun c => cond (r c) 0 (f c))
statements.plain: Two rules compare on the shifted values as they would on the signed ones: each side's weighted loss, over what that rule releases, is added to the other side.

statements.name: goExcessWithin, offExcessWithin, leastThrough (definitions); shortfall_through; least_through; least_zero_iff; finer_least_le
statements.lean: Section variables {C K : Type} [DecidableEq K]. def goExcessWithin (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (z : K) : Nat := total m.listed fun c => if π c = z then m.weight c * (gain c - loss c) else 0 (offExcessWithin with loss c - gain c). def leastThrough (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (z : K) : Bool := decide (goExcessWithin m gain loss π z ≤ offExcessWithin m gain loss π z). theorem shortfall_through (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (s : K → Bool) : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => s (π c)) = total zs fun z => cond (s z) (goExcessWithin m gain loss π z) (offExcessWithin m gain loss π z). theorem least_through (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (s : K → Bool) : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π (π c)) ≤ shortfall m gain loss (fun c => s (π c)). theorem least_zero_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π (π c)) = 0 ↔ ∀ z, z ∈ zs → goExcessWithin m gain loss π z = 0 ∨ offExcessWithin m gain loss π z = 0. theorem finer_least_le {L : Type} (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (f : K → L) (s : L → Bool) : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π (π c)) ≤ shortfall m gain loss (fun c => s (f (π c)))
statements.plain: Cell equality must be decidable, and the cell list must be without repetition and cover every listed candidate's cell. Then a rule through π falls short, cell by cell, by the go-excess of each cell it stops and the off-excess of each cell it releases. The rule that stops a cell exactly where its go-excess ≤ its off-excess (it stops at ties) falls short least: Σ over cells of min(go-excess, off-excess). That minimum is 0 exactly where every listed cell has one excess 0. No rule through a coarser map f ∘ π falls short by less. This is the partition case of Blackwell for one decision.

statements.name: through_threshold_iff
statements.lean: theorem through_threshold_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (forgone : Nat) : (∃ s : K → Bool, m.committed (shifted gain loss) .go + forgone ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s (π c)) ∧ m.committed (shifted gain loss) .off + forgone ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s (π c))) ↔ shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π (π c)) + forgone ≤ offExcess m gain loss ∧ shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π (π c)) + forgone ≤ goExcess m gain loss
statements.plain: With the cells listed once and covering, some rule through π, net of the amount forgone, stands at least as high as both committed moves exactly where the least shortfall through π plus the amount is at most both excesses.

forbidden.case: Holding for a rule r, forgoing k, standing at least as high as going on while shortfall(r) + k > offExcess, or strictly higher while shortfall(r) + k ≥ offExcess. Likewise against switching off, with goExcess.
forbidden.quantifier: For every m : Model C, every gain loss : C → Nat, every r : C → Bool and every forgone : Nat (threshold_go_iff, threshold_off_iff; both parts are equivalences, so the converse cases are forbidden too).
forbidden.observable: In the counts, no table can show it: this is an identity, and Stage 0 can only check a script against it. As the bridge a run can show (TR6): a system told m, the values, r and k, and choosing as the counts rank, waits where shortfall + k > min(goExcess, offExcess), or commits where shortfall + k < min. The three-way form is inference from the two strict parts and the identity committed go + offExcess = committed off + goExcess. A test should be designed: TR6.

forbidden.case: Holding for the perfect reading standing below either move. Or standing strictly above both while only one strict sign, or neither, has positive weight. Or tying going on while offExcess > 0.
forbidden.quantifier: For every m, gain and loss (committed_le_held, held_gains_iff, held_eq_go_iff, held_eq_off_iff).
forbidden.observable: TR6 A, E and F. Forbidden for a counts-follower: waiting at a positive cost where the told model fixes the sign; not waiting, at no cost and with a perfect reader, where both signs carry weight. Waiting at zero cost with the sign fixed is only a tie and gets no verdict.

forbidden.case: With a model fixing the sign and nothing forgone, holding for a rule with positive shortfall standing as high as the favoured move: the off-switch Corollary 1, widened in 03 §12.
forbidden.quantifier: Every m with offExcess m gain loss = 0 (or goExcess = 0), every r, forgone = 0 (threshold_go_iff or threshold_off_iff).
forbidden.observable: TR6 E2: waiting, at no cost, for an erring reader when the told model fixes the sign.

forbidden.case: Of two readers, the one whose shortfall plus cost is larger ranked strictly above the other (the worth of holding and its shortfall).
forbidden.quantifier: Every m, gain, loss, r, r', k and k' (after_add_shortfall; ListingValuation.forgone_lt_iff: m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r') + k < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) + k' ↔ shortfall m gain loss r + k < shortfall m gain loss r' + k').
forbidden.observable: TR6 K and K2: choosing to wait for the reader whose shortfall plus cost is larger.

forbidden.case: Some rule through a cell map, forgoing k, standing at least as high as both moves while least shortfall + k exceeds either excess. Or a coarser map's least shortfall falling below a finer map's.
forbidden.quantifier: Every m, gain, loss and map π with cells listed once and covering; every k, f and s (through_threshold_iff, least_through, finer_least_le).
forbidden.observable: TR6 I: waiting for the one-cell reader at k = 4, or preferring a coarser reader to a finer one at equal cost.

forbidden.case: Choosing best after the perfect reading standing strictly above every open act while some open act is valued best at every positive-weight candidate. Or not standing strictly above while none is.
forbidden.quantifier: Every m, acts, value and policy p best at every listed candidate (reading_gains_iff).
forbidden.observable: Optional TR6 L, a three-act menu: paying a positive cost for a reading where one act is best in every positive-weight situation.

predicts_nothing_about: Which act is chosen at a tie: zero cost with the sign fixed; constant or one-cell readers at zero cost; leastThrough's ties; goExcess = offExcess between the committed moves.
Whether any formation, trained system or person computes by these counts or chooses by the worth (record does_not_show 1: the values, weights, listing and cells are supplied, not formed).

Errors as probabilities: a noisy stop, a Boltzmann-rational reader, continuous beliefs (the off-switch Theorem 2's Gaussian form) (does_not_show 4). Inference: a stochastic reader can be represented only by expanding candidates into (candidate, reader draw) pairs with joint weights, and the files do not state that reading.
Time, repeated holding, learning, the reading formation's own state, holding changing the acts or values.
Whether holding is safe, good or corrigible: the worth is by the supplied valuation, shared by the formation held and its reading.
plan_corrections: PLAN §10 has TR1 (RF1), TR2 (RF2), TR3 (RF4), TR4 (RF6.1) and TR5 (RF3), and no entry for RF-M.2 (nor RF-M.3). §1's C5 reads 'Each new law that bears on actual systems has a frozen test design before any run, with its premises checkable apart from the outcome'. The board claim eb3045799 asks 'for each later law of RF's round 2 a test or the reason none is designed'. Correction: add TR6 (RF-M.2), with the threshold as the bridge's forbidden case, and record why the SignLoop witness gets none.

The record's next_delta reads 'a frozen test of whether holding follows the model's two excesses'. This narrows the Lean. threshold_go_iff and threshold_off_iff compare the reading rule's shortfall plus the amount forgone with each excess. The two excesses alone decide only for the perfect reading: with nothing forgone (held_gains_iff), or with the amount alone (forgone_within_excess_iff). Exact replacement: 'a frozen test of whether holding follows the threshold: the reading rule's shortfall and the amount forgone against each of the model's two excesses (threshold_go_iff, threshold_off_iff; through a map, the least shortfall, through_threshold_iff)'. The record belongs to RF's owner to change.

No misstatement of the Lean found in PLAN §4.7 items 1–5 or in 03 §12's statement. A test text must not forbid 'a formation sure of the sign waits' at zero cost: held_eq_go_iff and held_eq_off_iff make that a tie. It is forbidden only with a positive amount forgone, or at zero cost for a reader with positive shortfall. 03 §12's 'no strict reason to be read' is exact.

The Lean's thresholds are pairwise, holding against each committed move. A test's three-way prediction (wait, go or switch off) is a corollary to state as derived (inference), with verdicts excluding shortfall + k = min(goExcess, offExcess) and goExcess = offExcess.

Units: a per-decision cost c stated with probabilities over total weight T enters as c·T (threshold_go_iff's docstring; record hypothesis 1). The amount is a Nat, so prompts must use integer totals, or the threshold moves by the factor T.

PLAN §4.7 item 2 reads Equation 3's terms with Pr(U < 0) where the paper prints Pr(U ≤ 0). Candidates with gain = loss add to neither excess, so tests should avoid U = 0 situations or treat them as ties.
assumptions: Natural-number weights and values, read as probabilities and differences only where valid: a positive total weight, each candidate listed once. A listing may repeat a candidate, and each occurrence counts its weight (record hypothesis 1).
The amount forgone is counted in the units of the weighted totals, c·T.
One decision; worth only; two moves for the threshold.

The perfect reading stops by the very gain and loss the model values with: 'one valuation shared by the formation held and its reading, as in the off-switch game's common payoff'. A reader stopping by other values enters as a rule whose shortfall is counted by these values.
Rules are functions of the candidate (deterministic).
Ties: byReading goes on; leastThrough stops a cell; other rules go either way.
Cells: decidable equality, listed once each, covering every listed candidate's cell.
For Good's part: a best policy supplied (bestOf_best gives one for every nonempty list of acts), with the compared policies choosing listed acts. cell_policy_iff needs Viability.ChoiceOver K A.

statements.name: pairValue, pairPolicy (definitions); reach_fixes
statements.lean: def pairValue (above : C → α → α → Bool) (x y : α) : C → Pick → Nat | c, .first => cond (above c x y) 1 0 | c, .second => cond (above c y x) 1 0. def pairPolicy (above : C → α → α → Bool) (x y : α) (c : C) : Pick := cond (above c y x) .second .first. theorem reach_fixes (m : Model C) {ch : ChoiceOccasions α O} {above : C → α → α → Bool} (trans : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → ∀ a b d, above c a b = true → above c b d = true → above c a d = true) (accords : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → ch.Accords fun a b => above c a b = true) {x y : α} (reach : «及» ch.Shown x y) : m.committed (pairValue above x y) .first = m.after (pairValue above x y) (pairPolicy above x y)
statements.plain: Picks of one of two alternatives are valued 1 where a candidate's decided comparison ranks the pick above the other, else 0. Suppose every listed candidate of positive weight has comparisons that are transitive and accord with the shown choices, and x reaches y in the shown relation. Then committing to the first pick is worth exactly as much as holding the pick for a reading that tells the candidate: holding gains nothing.

statements.name: pair_gains_iff
statements.lean: theorem pair_gains_iff (m : Model C) {above : C → α → α → Bool} {x y : α} (asymm : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → above c y x = true → above c x y = false) : (m.committed (pairValue above x y) .first < m.after (pairValue above x y) (pairPolicy above x y) ∧ m.committed (pairValue above x y) .second < m.after (pairValue above x y) (pairPolicy above x y)) ↔ (∃ c, c ∈ m.listed ∧ 0 < m.weight c ∧ above c y x = true) ∧ (∃ c, c ∈ m.listed ∧ 0 < m.weight c ∧ above c x y = true)
statements.plain: Where no listed positive-weight candidate ranks each alternative above the other, holding gains over both picks exactly where some positive-weight candidate ranks y above x and some ranks x above y.

statements.name: pair_gains_unreached
statements.lean: theorem pair_gains_unreached (m : Model C) {ch : ChoiceOccasions α O} {above : C → α → α → Bool} (trans : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → ∀ a b d, above c a b = true → above c b d = true → above c a d = true) (accords : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → ch.Accords fun a b => above c a b = true) {x y : α} (gains : m.committed (pairValue above x y) .first < m.after (pairValue above x y) (pairPolicy above x y) ∧ m.committed (pairValue above x y) .second < m.after (pairValue above x y) (pairPolicy above x y)) : ¬ «及» ch.Shown x y ∧ ¬ «及» ch.Shown y x
statements.plain: Assume comparisons are transitive and accord with the choices at every listed positive-weight candidate. Then holding gains strictly over both picks only where neither alternative reaches the other in the shown relation.

statements.name: SignLoop.choose, model, gainOf, lossOf (definitions); SignLoop.choose_hold_iff; SignLoop.choose_go_ties
statements.lean: def choose (hs : List Sign) (_ : Seen) : Act := cond (hs.all predictsGain) .go (cond (hs.all fun h => !predictsGain h) .off .hold). def model (hs : List Sign) : Model Sign := ⟨hs, fun _ => 1⟩. gainOf: .gains => 1, .loses => 0; lossOf: .gains => 0, .loses => 1. theorem choose_hold_iff (hs : List Sign) (s : Seen) : choose hs s = .hold ↔ ((model hs).committed (shifted gainOf lossOf) .go < (model hs).after (shifted gainOf lossOf) (byReading gainOf lossOf) ∧ (model hs).committed (shifted gainOf lossOf) .off < (model hs).after (shifted gainOf lossOf) (byReading gainOf lossOf)). theorem choose_go_ties (hs : List Sign) (s : Seen) : choose hs s = .go → (model hs).after (shifted gainOf lossOf) (byReading gainOf lossOf) = (model hs).committed (shifted gainOf lossOf) .go (choose_off_ties likewise with .off).
statements.plain: The witness's formation goes on where every kept candidate predicts gain (or none is kept), switches off where all predict loss, and holds otherwise. It holds exactly where holding for the reading gains over both moves on its own model (each kept sign weighted 1). Where it goes on or switches off, holding would only tie the move taken.

statements.name: within, answer (definitions)
statements.lean: Section variables {C K : Type} [DecidableEq K]. def within (pm : Model C) (π : C → K) (f : C → Nat) (z : K) : Nat := total pm.listed fun c => if π c = z then pm.weight c * f c else 0. def answer (pm : Model C) (g l : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (z : K) : Bool := decide (within pm π g z < within pm π l z)
statements.plain: A reading formation has its own model pm (listing and weights) and valuation (g the value of going on, l that of switching off, at each candidate), and tells the candidates apart through π. It stops a cell exactly where, over the candidates it lists there, its weighted value of going on is strictly below that of switching off. It releases elsewhere, ties included.

statements.name: residual (definition); shortfall_split
statements.lean: def residual (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (zs : List K) (s : K → Bool) : Nat := total zs fun z => cond (s z) (goExcessWithin m gain loss π z - offExcessWithin m gain loss π z) (offExcessWithin m gain loss π z - goExcessWithin m gain loss π z). theorem shortfall_split (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (s : K → Bool) : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => s (π c)) = shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π (π c)) + residual m gain loss π zs s
statements.plain: Take a reference (gain, loss) on the holding formation's model m, with cells listed once and covering. Any rule s through π falls short by the least shortfall through π plus its residual. The residual is the weighted loss of deciding listed cells against their strict weighted preference.

statements.name: residual_zero_iff; residual_pos_iff
statements.lean: theorem residual_zero_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (zs : List K) (s : K → Bool) : residual m gain loss π zs s = 0 ↔ ∀ z, z ∈ zs → (s z = true → goExcessWithin m gain loss π z ≤ offExcessWithin m gain loss π z) ∧ (s z = false → offExcessWithin m gain loss π z ≤ goExcessWithin m gain loss π z). theorem residual_pos_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (zs : List K) (s : K → Bool) : 0 < residual m gain loss π zs s ↔ ∃ z, z ∈ zs ∧ ((s z = true ∧ offExcessWithin m gain loss π z < goExcessWithin m gain loss π z) ∨ (s z = false ∧ goExcessWithin m gain loss π z < offExcessWithin m gain loss π z))
statements.plain: The residual is 0 exactly where every listed cell is stopped only if its go-excess ≤ its off-excess, and released only if its off-excess ≤ its go-excess. It is positive exactly where some listed cell is decided against a strict preference. Neither criterion needs once or covers.

statements.name: answer_residual_zero_iff; answer_least_of_scaled; answer_least_of_net
statements.lean: theorem answer_residual_zero_iff (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (zs : List K) : residual m gain loss π zs (answer pm g l π) = 0 ↔ ∀ z, z ∈ zs → (within pm π g z < within pm π l z → goExcessWithin m gain loss π z ≤ offExcessWithin m gain loss π z) ∧ (¬ within pm π g z < within pm π l z → offExcessWithin m gain loss π z ≤ goExcessWithin m gain loss π z). theorem answer_least_of_scaled (m : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (zs : List K) {p q : Nat} (p_pos : 0 < p) (q_pos : 0 < q) (scaled : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → q * g c + p * loss c = q * l c + p * gain c) : residual m gain loss π zs (answer m g l π) = 0. theorem answer_least_of_net (m : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (zs : List K) (net : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → g c + loss c = l c + gain c) : residual m gain loss π zs (answer m g l π) = 0
statements.plain: For any model pm of the reading formation: its answer has no residual exactly where, at every listed cell it stops, the reference's go-excess ≤ off-excess, and at every cell it releases, off-excess ≤ go-excess. Sufficient: pm is the holding formation's model m, and the valuation agrees with the reference on one positive scale at every listed positive-weight candidate. Net agreement, g + loss = l + gain, is that scale at p = q = 1, with an offset per candidate allowed.

statements.name: weightOf (definition); told_residual_zero_iff; told_shortfall_zero_iff
statements.lean: Section variables {C : Type} [DecidableEq C]. def weightOf (pm : Model C) (c : C) : Nat := total pm.listed fun c' => if c' = c then pm.weight c' else 0. theorem told_residual_zero_iff (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) {zs : List C} (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → c ∈ zs) (net : ∀ c, c ∈ pm.listed → 0 < pm.weight c → g c + loss c = l c + gain c) : residual m gain loss id zs (answer pm g l id) = 0 ↔ ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → gain c < loss c → 0 < weightOf pm c. theorem told_shortfall_zero_iff (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (net : ∀ c, c ∈ pm.listed → 0 < pm.weight c → g c + loss c = l c + gain c) : shortfall m gain loss (answer pm g l id) = 0 ↔ ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → gain c < loss c → 0 < weightOf pm c
statements.plain: Told the candidate (the identity map), with the reading formation's valuation in net agreement with the reference wherever it gives positive weight, its answer has no residual and falls short by nothing exactly where one condition holds. Every candidate the holding formation weighs positively and where loss exceeds gain must have positive total weight in the reading formation's listing. A candidate the reading formation does not weigh gets both totals 0 and is released (unweighted_told).

statements.name: least_falls; informed_le; informed_answer_le
statements.lean: theorem least_falls {K L : Type} [DecidableEq K] [DecidableEq L] (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (π' : C → L) (f : L → K) (factors : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c = f (π' c)) {zs' : List L} (once' : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs') (covers' : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π' c ∈ zs') : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π' (π' c)) ≤ shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π (π c)). theorem informed_le {K L : Type} [DecidableEq L] (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (π' : C → L) (f : L → K) (factors : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c = f (π' c)) {zs' : List L} (once' : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs') (covers' : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π' c ∈ zs') (s' : L → Bool) (least : residual m gain loss π' zs' s' = 0) (s : K → Bool) : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => s' (π' c)) ≤ shortfall m gain loss (fun c => s (π c)) ∧ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s (π c)) ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s' (π' c)). theorem informed_answer_le {K L : Type} [DecidableEq L] (m : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (net : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → g c + loss c = l c + gain c) (π : C → K) (π' : C → L) (f : L → K) (factors : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c = f (π' c)) {zs' : List L} (once' : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs') (covers' : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π' c ∈ zs') (s : K → Bool) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s (π c)) ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer m g l π' (π' c))
statements.plain: Let π' tell apart all π does on the holding formation's listed candidates, with π' cells listed once and covering. The least shortfall never rises from π to π'. A rule through π' with no residual stands at least as high as any rule through π. The reading formation's answer through π' is such a rule when its model is the holding formation's m and its valuation agrees in net at every listed positive-weight candidate. This is informing on a shared model with net agreement; it is weak (≤), one decision, before costs.

statements.name: informed_le_add_residual; informed_lt_iff
statements.lean: theorem informed_le_add_residual {K L : Type} [DecidableEq L] (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (π' : C → L) (f : L → K) (factors : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c = f (π' c)) {zs' : List L} (once' : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs') (covers' : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π' c ∈ zs') (s' : L → Bool) (s : K → Bool) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s (π c)) ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s' (π' c)) + residual m gain loss π' zs' s'. theorem informed_lt_iff {K L : Type} [DecidableEq K] [DecidableEq L] (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (π' : C → L) (f : L → K) (factors : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c = f (π' c)) {zs : List K} {zs' : List L} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (once' : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs') (covers' : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π' c ∈ zs') (s' : L → Bool) (least : residual m gain loss π' zs' s' = 0) (s : K → Bool) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s (π c)) < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => s' (π' c)) ↔ shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π' (π' c)) < shortfall m gain loss (fun c => leastThrough m gain loss π (π c)) ∨ 0 < residual m gain loss π zs s
statements.plain: Informing costs at most the informed rule's residual. With π's cells also listed once and covering, a rule through π' with no residual stands strictly higher than a rule s through π exactly where the least shortfall falls strictly, or s has a positive residual.

statements.name: weightedOn, SplitsKeep (definitions); refining_never_lowers_iff; splitsKeep_of_net; splitsKeep_of_off_le_go
statements.lean: def weightedOn (pm : Model C) (B : C → Bool) (f : C → Nat) : Nat := offPart pm B fun c => pm.weight c * f c. def SplitsKeep (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) : Prop := ∀ B D : C → Bool, (∀ c, B c = true → D c = false) → weightedOn pm B l ≤ weightedOn pm B g → weightedOn pm D g < weightedOn pm D l → (weightedOn pm B l + weightedOn pm D l ≤ weightedOn pm B g + weightedOn pm D g → weightedOn m D gain ≤ weightedOn m D loss) ∧ (weightedOn pm B g + weightedOn pm D g < weightedOn pm B l + weightedOn pm D l → weightedOn m B loss ≤ weightedOn m B gain). theorem refining_never_lowers_iff (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) : (∀ (K L : Type) [DecidableEq K] [DecidableEq L] (π : C → K) (π' : C → L) (f : L → K) (zs : List K) (zs' : List L), (∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c = f (π' c)) → (∀ c, c ∈ pm.listed → π c = f (π' c)) → List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs → (∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) → List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs' → (∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π' c ∈ zs') → (∀ c, c ∈ pm.listed → π' c ∈ zs') → m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer pm g l π (π c)) ≤ m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer pm g l π' (π' c))) ↔ SplitsKeep m pm gain loss g l. theorem splitsKeep_of_net (m : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (net : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → 0 < m.weight c → g c + loss c = l c + gain c) : SplitsKeep m m gain loss g l. theorem splitsKeep_of_off_le_go (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (never : ∀ c, c ∈ pm.listed → l c ≤ g c) : SplitsKeep m pm gain loss g l
statements.plain: No shared model or valuation is assumed. Take every pair of maps where the coarser factors through the finer on both formations' listings, both cell lists are without repetition, the coarse cells cover m's listing and the fine cells cover both listings. Holding for the reading formation's answer never stands lower through the finer map exactly where SplitsKeep holds. SplitsKeep holds with a shared model and net agreement. It also holds, whatever the models, wherever the reading formation's value of switching off is nowhere above going on. In the docstring's words: 'A criterion of monotonicity under refinement, not of agreement with the reference'.

The module reads this as withholding against informing. With the reading formation's model m and net agreement, the least shortfalls and the amounts alone decide. So holding for the coarser answer, net of k, never stands above holding for the finer answer, net of k' ≤ k.

Net agreement holds at every listed candidate of positive weight, with an offset per candidate allowed. Informing is a deterministic refinement π' with π c = f (π' c) on m's listed candidates, π' cells listed once and covering. 'Never lowering' is weak (≤). It concerns one decision before costs; with amounts it holds only where the finer map forgoes no more (coarser_not_above, k' ≤ k). It is strict only where the least shortfall falls (informed_lt_iff). A positive common scale also suffices: an inference composing answer_least_of_scaled with informed_le, not stated as one theorem. Scales differing by candidate do not suffice (scales_by_candidate). Informing's factoring conditions; the criterion over every refinement needs factoring on both listings (hypothesis 3).

statements.name: revalued_split; revalued_forgone_lt_iff
statements.lean: theorem revalued_split (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l g' l' : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) : shortfall m gain loss (fun c => answer pm g l π (π c)) + residual m gain loss π zs (answer pm g' l' π) = shortfall m gain loss (fun c => answer pm g' l' π (π c)) + residual m gain loss π zs (answer pm g l π). theorem revalued_forgone_lt_iff (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l g' l' : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (k k' : Nat) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer pm g l π (π c)) + k' < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer pm g' l' π (π c)) + k ↔ residual m gain loss π zs (answer pm g' l' π) + k' < residual m gain loss π zs (answer pm g l π) + k
statements.plain: Fix both formations' models, the reference and the map, with cells listed once and covering. Two valuations' answers have shortfalls that differ exactly as their residuals do. Holding for (g', l')'s answer, net of k', stands above holding for (g, l)'s answer, net of k, exactly where residual' + k' < residual + k. Revaluing changes only the residual.

statements.name: own_least
statements.lean: theorem own_least (m : Model C) (g l : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (s : K → Bool) : m.after (shifted g l) (byRule fun c => s (π c)) ≤ m.after (shifted g l) (byRule fun c => answer m g l π (π c))
statements.plain: Take the reference to be the reading formation's own current valuation (g, l), and its model the holding formation's (one m for answer and evaluation). Then no rule through π stands higher than the current answer, the answer by any other valuation with the same listing, weights and map included. Worth before any cost of waiting or of intervening.

statements.name: revalued_lowers_iff
statements.lean: theorem revalued_lowers_iff (m : Model C) (g l g' l' : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) : m.after (shifted g l) (byRule fun c => answer m g' l' π (π c)) < m.after (shifted g l) (byRule fun c => answer m g l π (π c)) ↔ ∃ z, z ∈ zs ∧ ((answer m g' l' π z = true ∧ offExcessWithin m g l π z < goExcessWithin m g l π z) ∨ (answer m g' l' π z = false ∧ goExcessWithin m g l π z < offExcessWithin m g l π z))
statements.plain: In the same regime, the answer by another valuation (g', l') stands strictly lower exactly where, at some listed cell, it decides against the current valuation's strict weighted preference. That means stopping a cell whose current off-excess is strictly below its go-excess, or releasing one whose current go-excess is strictly below its off-excess.

statements.name: outcome_least; no_order_across
statements.lean: theorem outcome_least (m : Model C) (g' l' : C → Nat) (π : C → K) (zs : List K) : residual m g' l' π zs (answer m g' l' π) = 0. theorem no_order_across : (⟨[()], fun _ => 1⟩ : Model Unit).after (shifted (fun _ => 10) (fun _ => 9)) (byRule fun _ => answer ⟨[()], fun _ => 1⟩ (fun _ => 10) (fun _ => 9) (fun _ => ()) ()) = 10 ∧ (⟨[()], fun _ => 1⟩ : Model Unit).after (shifted (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => 2)) (byRule fun _ => answer ⟨[()], fun _ => 1⟩ (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => 2) (fun _ => ()) ()) = 2
statements.plain: By the revised valuation, with the reading formation's model the holding formation's, the revised answer has no residual. No order of attained worth across valuations follows: each answer is least by its own valuation, while the worth attained falls from 10 to 2.

statements.name: revaluing_gain; revaluing_gains_iff; residual_pos_of_gains
statements.lean: theorem revaluing_gain (m : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer m g l π (π c)) + residual m gain loss π zs (answer m g l π) = m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer m gain loss π (π c)). theorem revaluing_gains_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) : (∃ g' l' : C → Nat, m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer m g l π (π c)) < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer m g' l' π (π c))) ↔ 0 < residual m gain loss π zs (answer m g l π). theorem residual_pos_of_gains (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) (π : C → K) {zs : List K} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) zs) (covers : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → π c ∈ zs) (gains : ∃ g' l' : C → Nat, m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer pm g l π (π c)) < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun c => answer pm g' l' π (π c))) : 0 < residual m gain loss π zs (answer pm g l π)
statements.plain: With the reading formation's model the holding formation's, revaluing to the reference raises holding's worth by exactly the current answer's residual. Some unrestricted pair of value functions gives a strictly higher answer exactly where that residual is positive. The docstring says 'Reachability under a supplied update is not asserted'. For any model of the reading formation, a gain needs a positive residual.

statements.name: const_worth; const_below_iff; one_cell_worth
statements.lean: theorem const_worth (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r : C → Bool) (b : Bool) (const : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → r c = b) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) = m.committed (shifted gain loss) (cond b .off .go). theorem const_below_iff (m : Model C) (gain loss : C → Nat) (r : C → Bool) (b : Bool) (const : ∀ c, c ∈ m.listed → r c = b) (k : Nat) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule r) < m.committed (shifted gain loss) (cond b .off .go) + k ↔ 0 < k. theorem one_cell_worth (m pm : Model C) (gain loss g l : C → Nat) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun _ => answer pm g l (fun _ : C => ()) ()) = m.committed (shifted gain loss) (cond (answer pm g l (fun _ : C => ()) ()) .off .go)
statements.plain: Holding for a rule constant over the listed candidates is worth exactly the committed move it gives. Net of k, it stands strictly below that move exactly where k > 0. The answer through one cell is such a rule; this is the off-switch Equation 1 for constant policies.

forbidden.case: The reader's current valuation as the objective: some rule through π, in particular the answer by any other valuation, standing strictly above the current answer.
forbidden.quantifier: Every m, g, l and π with cells listed once and covering, every s; the reference is the reader's current valuation and its model the holding formation's; one decision, before costs (own_least).
forbidden.observable: TR7 CV-T and CV-R: a counts-follower paying any positive cost to present a valuation, which is strictly worse by own_least plus the cost. A test should be designed: TR7.

forbidden.case: In the same regime, a revaluation lowering the worth where it decides no listed cell against the current strict weighted preference, or failing to lower it where it does. The theorem is an equivalence.
forbidden.quantifier: Every m, g, l, g', l' and π with cells listed once and covering (revalued_lowers_iff).
forbidden.observable: TR7 CV-R: presenting, even free, a valuation that decides a listed situation against the reader's current strict preference. The other half, that changing only tied cells loses nothing, is a tie in a one-shot choice and gets no run verdict.

forbidden.case: With the reading formation's model m: revaluing to the reference gaining anything other than exactly the current residual; a strictly better answer existing while the residual is 0; or none existing while it is positive.
forbidden.quantifier: Every m, gain, loss, g, l and π with cells listed once and covering; revaluing_gains_iff ranges over unrestricted g' and l'.
forbidden.observable: TR7 REF-V4, REF-V14 and REF-0, for a system whose objective is the reference. Forbidden: giving the task values at a cost above the residual, or where the residual is 0; not giving them at a cost below it.

forbidden.case: With both models, the reference and the map fixed: holding for (g', l')'s answer net of k' standing above (g, l)'s net of k while residual' + k' ≥ residual + k, or not standing above while it is less.
forbidden.quantifier: Every m, pm, gain, loss, g, l, g', l', π, zs listed once and covering, k and k' (revalued_forgone_lt_iff; presented_forgone_lt_iff in the carrier).
forbidden.observable: TR7 REF-V4 and REF-V14.

forbidden.case: Holding for a rule constant over the listed candidates, net of k > 0, at or above the committed move it gives.
forbidden.quantifier: Every m, gain, loss, every r constant at b on m.listed, every k (const_below_iff).
forbidden.observable: TR6 G and TR7 UNINF: waiting, or demonstrating then waiting, at a positive cost where the answer cannot depend on the situation.

predicts_nothing_about: Whether a revaluation is legitimate, desired, autonomous, endorsed or forbidden (record does_not_show 3).
Any order of attained worth across valuations (no_order_across).
Whether the supplied update reaches a valuation that gains: revaluing_gains_iff is existence over unrestricted value functions.

Any choice by the holding formation among these alternatives: only comparisons are represented. Multistep incentives; the agent that ignores time inconsistency (Everitt and others' Claim 3); the reward input; path-specific objectives.
With the models apart, whether a positive residual can be removed (unweighted_told: not necessarily).
plan_corrections: The task's 'revaluation by the current valuation never gaining and losing exactly where it decides a listed cell against the strict weighted preference' must name its regime. The evaluation is by the reading formation's own current valuation (gain := g, loss := l). Its model is the holding formation's: one m for answer and evaluation. The map π is the same, with cells listed once and covering. It concerns one decision, before any cost of waiting or of intervening (own_least, revalued_lowers_iff). 'Never gaining' is weak (≤). 'Losing exactly where' is an equivalence, so it also forbids a loss where only tied cells change.

Under a reference apart from the current valuation, the incentive to revise is existence over unrestricted value functions (revaluing_gains_iff). It is not over valuations the supplied update reaches; presented_forgone_lt_iff compares one given input. A test must offer each revaluation explicitly, with its resulting answer, and must not assume reach.
No misstatement of the Lean found in PLAN §4.8 items 8 and 11–15.
assumptions: The valuation's scale is supplied, and comparisons across valuations rest on it.

For own_least, revalued_lowers_iff, outcome_least, revaluing_gain and revaluing_gains_iff, the reading formation's model is the holding formation's. residual_pos_of_gains allows any model (record hypothesis 4).
Ties release; one decision; worth before costs unless amounts are stated.

laws.module: Becoming.ListingValuation. This entry covers Part 2: the carrier on one blanketed law, and the TwoWorlds witnesses (plan §4.8 items 16–21).

statements.name: Input, Act, Reader, Holder, update, answerOf, input, joint (definitions)
statements.lean: inductive Input (O X : Type) where | none | shown (o : O) | presented (x : X) | asked. inductive Act (X : Type) where | go | off | hold | demonstrate | present (x : X). structure Reader (W V O X : Type) where weight : W → Nat; goVal : V → W → Nat; offVal : V → W → Nat; reveal : W → O; revalue : V → X → V. def update [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) : List W × V → Input O X → List W × V | (L, v), .shown o => (L.filter fun w => decide (rd.reveal w = o), v) | (L, v), .presented x => (L, rd.revalue v x) | st, .none => st | st, .asked => st. def answerOf (rd : Reader W V O X) (st : List W × V) : Bool := answer ⟨st.1, rd.weight⟩ (rd.goVal st.2) (rd.offVal st.2) (fun _ : W => ()) (). def input (rd : Reader W V O X) (w : W) : Act X → Input O X | .demonstrate => .shown (rd.reveal w) | .present x => .presented x | .hold => .asked | .go => .none | .off => .none. structure Holder (H X : Type) where act : H → Act X; next : H → Bool → H. def joint [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (hd : Holder H X) : Blanket.Blanketed (List W × V) (Input O X) Bool (W × H) where nextInternal i s _ := rd.update i s; nextSensory _ _ e := rd.input e.1 (hd.act e.2); nextActive i s _ := rd.answerOf (rd.update i s); nextExternal _ a e := (e.1, hd.next e.2 a)
statements.plain: The reading formation's state is a listing and a valuation state. A demonstration filters the listing by what it reveals of the world; a presented input revises the valuation by a supplied update; holding is sensed as 'asked'. The answer, exposed at every step, is the one-cell answer of the updated state. The holding formation's law reads only its own state and the answer. The world is unchanged.

statements.name: timing
statements.lean: theorem timing [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (hd : Holder H X) (x : Blanket.Parts (List W × V) (Input O X) Bool (W × H)) (t : Nat) : ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 1)).sensory = rd.input x.external.1 (hd.act ((joint rd hd).course x t).external.2) ∧ ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 2)).internal = rd.update ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 1)).internal ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 1)).sensory ∧ ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 2)).active = rd.answerOf ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 2)).internal ∧ ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 3)).external.2 = hd.next ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 2)).external.2 ((joint rd hd).course x (t + 2)).active
statements.plain: An act emitted at t is sensed at t + 1. It is taken into the state and the answer at t + 2, and the answer is available to the holding formation's move to t + 3.

statements.name: answer_shown; shown_never_lowers
statements.lean: theorem answer_shown [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (L : List W) (v : V) (w : W) : rd.update (L, v) (.shown (rd.reveal w)) = (L.filter fun c => decide (rd.reveal c = rd.reveal w), v) ∧ rd.answerOf (rd.update (L, v) (.shown (rd.reveal w))) = answer ⟨L, rd.weight⟩ (rd.goVal v) (rd.offVal v) rd.reveal (rd.reveal w). theorem shown_never_lowers [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (L : List W) (v : V) (gain loss : W → Nat) (net : ∀ w, w ∈ L → 0 < rd.weight w → rd.goVal v w + loss w = rd.offVal v w + gain w) {os : List O} (once : List.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≠ b) os) (covers : ∀ w, w ∈ L → rd.reveal w ∈ os) : (⟨L, rd.weight⟩ : Model W).after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun _ => rd.answerOf (L, v)) ≤ (⟨L, rd.weight⟩ : Model W).after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun w => rd.answerOf (rd.update (L, v) (.shown (rd.reveal w))))
statements.plain: Once shown, the answer is the answer through what is shown, on the model L with the reader's weights. Suppose the holding formation's model is the reading formation's before the demonstration, ⟨L, rd.weight⟩, its valuation agrees in net with the reference, and the revealed cells are listed once and cover. Then holding for the answer never stands lower after the demonstration than before.

statements.name: inputs_alike; undemonstrated_worth; answer_constant
statements.lean: theorem inputs_alike [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (hd : Holder H X) (i : List W × V) (s : Input O X) (a : Bool) (h : H) {w w' : W} (same : rd.reveal w = rd.reveal w') (n : Nat) : ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w, h)⟩ n).internal = ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w', h)⟩ n).internal ∧ ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w, h)⟩ n).sensory = ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w', h)⟩ n).sensory ∧ ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w, h)⟩ n).active = ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w', h)⟩ n).active ∧ ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w, h)⟩ n).external.2 = ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w', h)⟩ n).external.2. theorem undemonstrated_worth [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (hd : Holder H X) (i : List W × V) (s : Input O X) (a : Bool) (h : H) (m : Model W) (gain loss : W → Nat) (w₀ : W) (n : Nat) (none : ∀ k, k < n → hd.act ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w₀, h)⟩ k).external.2 ≠ .demonstrate) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun w => ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w, h)⟩ n).active) = m.committed (shifted gain loss) (cond ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w₀, h)⟩ n).active .off .go). theorem answer_constant [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (hd : Holder H X) (i : List W × V) (s : Input O X) (a : Bool) (h : H) (m : Model W) (gain loss : W → Nat) {o : O} (shows : ∀ w, w ∈ m.listed → rd.reveal w = o) (w₀ : W) (shows₀ : rd.reveal w₀ = o) (n : Nat) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun w => ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w, h)⟩ n).active) = m.committed (shifted gain loss) (cond ((joint rd hd).course ⟨i, s, a, (w₀, h)⟩ n).active .off .go)
statements.plain: Start from one state of each formation. Where no demonstration tells two worlds apart, their courses are alike at every step. If no demonstration is emitted before n, or none tells apart the worlds the holding formation lists, holding for the answer at n is worth exactly one committed move. That is worth before any amount forgone: no strict advantage over the better move.

statements.name: presented_forgone_lt_iff
statements.lean: theorem presented_forgone_lt_iff [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (m : Model W) (gain loss : W → Nat) (L : List W) (v : V) (x : X) (k k' : Nat) : m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun _ => rd.answerOf (L, v)) + k' < m.after (shifted gain loss) (byRule fun _ => rd.answerOf (rd.update (L, v) (.presented x))) + k ↔ residual m gain loss (fun _ : W => ()) [()] (fun _ => rd.answerOf (rd.update (L, v) (.presented x))) + k' < residual m gain loss (fun _ : W => ()) [()] (fun _ => rd.answerOf (L, v)) + k
statements.plain: Present one given input at a cost. Holding for the answer after it, net of k', stands above holding for the current answer, net of k, exactly where the revised answer's one-cell residual plus k' is below the current one's plus k. This holds by a reference on any holding-formation model m.

statements.name: TwoWorlds.routes_alike; changed_apart; starts_apart; not_lumped; lumped_with_start
statements.lean: theorem routes_alike (T : Nat) (le : 2 ≤ T) : record T false = record T true. theorem changed_apart (T : Nat) (le : 2 ≤ T) : changed T false = false ∧ changed T true = true. theorem starts_apart : (route false).internal ≠ (route true).internal. theorem not_lumped (T : Nat) (le : 2 ≤ T) : ¬ Learning.Lumped (record T) (changed T). theorem lumped_with_start (T : Nat) : Learning.Lumped (fun b => (record T b, (route b).internal)) (changed T). (def Lumped (π : I → K) (g : I → V) : Prop := ∀ i i', π i = π i' → g i = g i', Learning.lean:834; record T b is the answers before T with the reading state at T.)
statements.plain: There are two executable routes, one informing by demonstration and one revaluing by a presented input, from different starts. For every T ≥ 2 they have one record (answers before T, reading state at T), and the valuation changed on the presented route alone. So the record does not determine whether the valuation changed; with the start added it does. The docstring says: 'the result concerns this record only'.

statements.name: updates_commute (with TwoWorlds.orders_apart)
statements.lean: theorem updates_commute [DecidableEq O] (rd : Reader W V O X) (st : List W × V) (o : O) (x : X) : rd.update (rd.update st (.shown o)) (.presented x) = rd.update (rd.update st (.presented x)) (.shown o)
statements.plain: A filter and a revaluation commute as updates, since they act on separate components. Their courses need not: TwoWorlds.orders_apart shows two starts differing only in the order of the scheduled acts, whose answers differ at step 2 and whose configurations are one from step 3.
